OPEN with a red-first suite already pinned: #71 (30 pinned rows, test/orchestrator-wake-red.test.mjs), #164 (10 pinned rows, test/blind-waits-red.test.mjs), #320 (1 pinned row, test/swarm-wake.test.mjs). OPEN, needs a lane: #65 the ~60s keyed-wave close stall on the approval path has no fix and no test; #128 the provider-webhook push machinery exists (coordinator.mjs:5248, hmac-advisory-webhook.mjs) but no HTTPS route mounts it (no 'webhook' in web-northbound.mjs); #255 interaction events still reach no coordination row (the projection reads them at application-observation.mjs:543); #175 the interpreter's semantics are 'the named roles are the trigger, the remaining members receive' (workflow-interpreter.mjs:927-938) and the campaign briefs use them that way, so the issue's case (naming the recipient in roles) needs the key documented or split into an explicit recipients field; #50 partially: omp surfaces a stalled transport as an observation instead of a silent hang (omp-rpc.mjs:11-46,606), the adapter-level turn error and pre-TTL rotation are not landed. NEEDS DESIGN (a doc and pins before code): #56 the worker-visible stall clock and liveness channel, #181 signal recipients parked alive until delivery, #188 failure-stall to forced review, #274 the swarm visibility model (its first finding is partially delivered: #464 caps the participant row's role at the objective's first line, swarm-state.mjs:1216; the root still holds no participant row, swarm-runtime.mjs:250).

items.change: docs/55-failure-stall.md is the design an implementation lane builds red-first: (1) the fact - the failure-stall count is the number of CONSECUTIVE failure verdicts of a run in ledger order, folded in the same derivation that already carries progressClass and the terminal cause, a success verdict resetting it, never a clock (the #163 law); (2) the park - one durable run.parked {reason, count, threshold, atSeq} row at the deployment-declared threshold, stopping NEW spawns, never stopping, killing or interrupting a live member, never writing a terminal phase, clearing only by the orchestrator's answer or a later success verdict; (3) the attention item - exactly one failure_stall row per park, carrying the counted verdicts in ledger order with each attempt's death certificate (the evidence the failure path already records, no second store); (4) the wake reason - failure_stall joins the closed WAKE_REASONS set after issue #71's set is on the tree, because that test pins the set; (5) the threshold - operator policy stallPolicy.failureCount, unset means the park never fires, recorded in limits.mjs, bounds no action; and (6) seven red-first pins (FS-1..FS-7) plus the migration (the ninth attention kind with the docs/36 7.4 regeneration, the run view's failureStall field, the spawn-gate refusal in runtime-admission.mjs).

needsFromOthers: An independent check of this design against docs/50's law set and #258's ruling (the threshold must bound no action) before an implementation lane is staffed; the root's check is the independent one, and this seat's own review of it is recorded honestly as the author's.
